preprocessing.source: original PNG at image_relpath (pixels only; no mask, bbox or metadata)
preprocessing.color: single grayscale channel, 8 bit (mode 'L'); other modes are rejected
preprocessing.geometry: whole image scaled down proportionally to fit (PIL.ImageOps.contain), centred on a black canvas; no crop, no stretch
preprocessing.side_rounding: Pillow rounds the scaled side with Python round() (half to even)
preprocessing.centering: offset = (target - scaled) // 2; an odd remainder lies right/bottom
preprocessing.scaling: float32(uint8) / 255 -> [0, 1]; fixed, nothing estimated from data
preprocessing.flatten: none - the CNN receives the image array, no flattening transformation
preprocessing.rescaling_in_model: none; the division by 255 happens exactly once in this preparation

architecture: input 160x160x1 float32 in [0, 1] (division by 255 happens once in the data preparation)
RandomFlip('horizontal', seed=42) - active only while training
Dense 1, sigmoid (output) - the output IS the malignant score
configuration.train_shuffle: tf.data shuffle over the whole train set, seed 42, reshuffled every epoch

evaluation.rule: score >= threshold; no optimisation or calibration

probe.data: first 16 TRAIN images in stable order

gpu.memory_note: TensorFlow allocator statistics and nvidia-smi values observed in this run; no memory limit was set by the project

environment_report.note: read only; it does not prove this process's environment

limitations: One fixed holdout, one seed and one run: no variance estimate, no significance statement.
Resolution, model family and augmentation differ from the LogReg baseline; the comparison is between whole pipelines.
Training curves (flip, dropout) and validation curves (inference mode) are computed under different conditions.
The seed supports traceability; byte-identical GPU training runs are not promised.
The horizontal flip keeps the class but does not remove burned-in markers or device cues.
Scores are sigmoid outputs, not shown to be calibrated disease probabilities; the 0.5 threshold is a fixed convention.
Train-set metrics only describe the fit to the training data.
